clue.text: Clueless chairman's annoyed interjection

definitions.meaning: Humphrey Lyttelton, known as ..., chaired the BBC radio panel game I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue
a grunt or snort of irritation or disbelief

explanation.surface: A bumbling chairman mutters crossly at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Clueless is a playful nod to I'm Sorry I Haven't a Clue, a long-running BBC Radio 4 comedy panel show whose chairman was jazz trumpeter Humphrey Lyttelton.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a sound of doubt or irritation, the very noise an annoyed person makes.

clue.text: Ambitious, like Icarus before meltdown?

definitions.meaning: aiming high, striving for great success
Icarus soared near the Sun until the wax of his wings melted

explanation.surface: An ambitious person is compared to Icarus before his fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-flying person is very ambitious, and Icarus literally flew high before falling.

clue.text: Low state of mind daughter's shaken off

indicators.note: the daughter is shaken off, so her letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a mood is a state of mind
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A gloomy frame of mind after a daughter leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Low looks like an adjective for depressed; it is the noise a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A low is the deep sound a cow makes, which is its moo.

clue.text: Sharpens tip of toothpick — really!

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it

indicators.note: the tip of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens a toothpick, and exclaims about it.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation, honest! means truly or really.

clue.text: Rogue caught crony dipping into spoils

indicators.note: the caught-plus-crony pair dips inside the word for spoils, so it is placed within it

parts.note: swag is loot or plunder
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
an ally is a friend or close associate

explanation.surface: A villain's accomplice helps himself to the stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a mischievous rascal, which is exactly the sense of this jaunty word.

clue.text: Oil producer's impudence about a priest in S Africa

indicators.note: the impudence word goes about, around, the rest

parts.note: sass is cheek or impudence

indicators.note: the a-and-priest pair sits inside the letters for South Africa

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: An oil company boss is cheeky about a cleric in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives SAFRA, which 'about' wraps: the cheek word splits after its third letter to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sassafras tree yields an aromatic oil from its bark and roots.

clue.text: Half of TV series on a Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down clue the A goes on, below, the first piece
taking the first half of the series title

parts.note: 'Allo 'Allo! is a British sitcom set in wartime France

explanation.surface: Half a television series is filmed in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allo 'Allo! was a popular BBC comedy series of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in Clackmannanshire, central Scotland.

clue.text: Sucker picking up ball in middle of game

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up means the whole is read upwards
the ball word goes into the centre of the game word

parts.note: pool is a cue game
a pill is slang for a ball

explanation.surface: A dupe collects a ball in the middle of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in middle of' gives POPILLOL, which 'picking up' turns upwards. Sucker looks like a dupe, but it is a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker is a sweet on a stick, sucked by children.

clue.text: Around this place, possibly what "will" mostly means

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed around the this-place word
possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: here means this place

explanation.surface: A lawyer explains what a will mostly means locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' makes WWITHAL from the five letters plus WIL ('mostly' trims the will word), and 'Around' wraps that about the place word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherewithal is the means or resources needed to do something.

clue.text: Noisily breathe air — quiet!

parts.note: air is a gas
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A command to stop breathing so loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to breathe in sharply and audibly.

clue.text: Plant the Spanish used with reason

parts.note: grounds are the reasons or justification for something
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone justifies the use of a Spanish plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used with' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common weed of the daisy family, a plant.

clue.text: Died among dregs in city

indicators.note: the abbreviation for died goes among the letters of the dregs word, so inside it

parts.note: lees are the sediment at the bottom of a wine barrel
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone died in squalor in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: Sweets one's found in display, bringing illusory happiness

parts.note: fools are fruit-and-cream desserts, and sweets is British for desserts

indicators.note: the one's piece is found inside the display word, so it is put within it

parts.note: a parade is a show or display
one is I, and 's is read as IS

explanation.surface: Someone finds bliss among a display of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of puréed fruit folded into cream; 'sweets' here means desserts. 'bringing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a state of happiness based on a false belief.

clue.text: Play of light nature, say, introduced by old friend

indicators.note: the old-friend pieces come first, introducing the rest

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken that sounds like the letters entered

parts.note: essence is the intrinsic nature of something

explanation.surface: An old friend brings up the nature of play under lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescence is a milky iridescent shimmer of colours, like an opal.

clue.text: Firmly established like luxury armchairs?

definitions.meaning: deeply rooted and hard to remove

explanation.surface: A firmly entrenched comfort of luxurious chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-seated means ingrained, and plush armchairs literally have deep seats.

clue.text: Period of revolution is long-no end in sight

indicators.note: the end of the word for long cannot be seen, so its last letter is removed

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: Someone longs hopelessly with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is the time the Earth takes to revolve once around the Sun.

clue.text: On which bouncers go to bar, disturbed by racket

indicators.note: the to-and-bar pair is broken into by the racket word, which sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a ramp is British slang for a swindle or racket
a line is a bar or stripe

explanation.surface: Nightclub doormen head to the bar, upset by the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncers suggests nightclub doormen, but here they are people bouncing up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is the springy sheet on which people bounce.

clue.text: Bungling mother protecting boy's right in Paris

indicators.note: the mother word wraps around the boy, so he goes inside it

parts.note: ma is mother
Al is a boy's name
droit is French for right

explanation.surface: A clumsy mother guards her son's legal rights in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy or inept, which is bungling.

clue.text: Unusually calm site -— could be the traveller's joy

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters are in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A strangely quiet site gives a traveller pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Traveller's joy is the common name of wild clematis; 'could be' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Traveller's joy is a wild species of the climbing plant genus, so the genus name covers it.

clue.text: Goads a tinker without justification

parts.note: to needle someone is to goad or provoke them
Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: Someone provokes a travelling mender for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinker looks like a generic itinerant mender; it points to a particular Shakespearean one.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something needlessly is doing it without good reason or need.

clue.text: Johnny's evidence of exposure as to cold

definitions.meaning: Johnny is informal British for a man or fellow

definitions.text: evidence of exposure as to cold
definitions.meaning: a sore crack in skin caused by cold wind

explanation.surface: A man's skin shows signs of having been out in the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap means a fellow, and also the roughening of skin from cold weather.

clue.text: Cowardly to act thus when in pain!

parts.words: to act thus when in pain
parts.note: to cry out loudly is to yell

parts.words: to act thus when in pain
parts.note: ow is the cry people give when hurt

explanation.surface: It is cowardly to cry out when hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as yell 'ow', what someone does when hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for cowardly or lacking courage.

clue.text: Key Tory put Archers' place in the shade

indicators.note: the village is put into the key-and-Tory pair, signalling a container
goes with put to place the village inside the other two pieces

parts.note: C is a musical key
blue is the colour of the Conservative Party, so a Tory is a blue
Ambridge is the fictional village in the BBC radio soap The Archers

explanation.surface: A prominent Conservative outshines a famous radio village.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC Radio 4 farming soap opera. 'Put in the shade' looks like an idiom for outshining.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge blue is a pale greenish-blue colour, a shade.

clue.text: Jumper worn by this writer's lover

indicators.note: the writer wears the jumper, so the writer is inside it

parts.note: a roo, kangaroo, is a jumper
the setter refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A sweater worn by the writer's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper looks like a British sweater, but it is a leaping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, Shakespeare's young lover, gives his name to any ardent suitor.

clue.text: Like Uncle Arly, say, raised in outskirts of Auckland

indicators.note: the raised piece goes inside the outskirts letters
the outskirts of the word are its first and last letters
in a down clue raised means the piece is read upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A relative brought up on the edge of an Auckland suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Arly is the old man of Edward Lear's poem Incidents in the Life of My Uncle Arly.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's Uncle Arly is an elderly man, so being old is like him.

clue.text: French novelist spotted in African savannah?

definitions.meaning: the author of Our Lady of the Flowers and The Thief's Journal
a spotted cat-like mammal of Africa

explanation.surface: A French writer is seen on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted looks like a verb meaning seen; it is an adjective describing the animal's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Jean Genet shares his surname with the spotted civet-like carnivore of Africa.

clue.text: Burn the midnight oil seeking name for sonata

definitions.meaning: to work late at night, here at a second job
Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 14 is popularly known by this name

explanation.surface: A composer works late into the night on a sonata's title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to work a second job, often at night; and Beethoven's famous sonata bears the name.

clue.text: Enterprising head abandoned Indian state

indicators.note: the head word is abandoned, taken out of the larger word

parts.note: go-ahead means enterprising or progressive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dynamic leader quits an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on India's west coast.

clue.text: Line up before film, sporting formal wear

indicators.note: the line-up word comes before the film word in the answer

parts.note: soldiers dress when they line up in formation
a coat is a thin layer or film

explanation.surface: Actors queue before shooting, wearing smart clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress coat is a man's tailcoat worn for formal evening occasions.

clue.text: Reportedly hold and use an area of woodland

indicators.note: this word tells us the answer is said like another word

parts.note: to wield a tool is to hold and use it

explanation.surface: Someone is said to hold and use a patch of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is an area of south-east England once heavily wooded.
explanation.definitionFit: A weald is an old word for wooded country, especially the Weald of Kent and Sussex.
